seo_keywords: MRCP Part 1, Royal College of Physicians, Internal Medicine, question bank, SBA, Passmed UK
content:
MRCP Part 1 Overview

The MRCP (Membership of the Royal Colleges of Physicians) Diploma is a postgraduate qualification awarded by the Federation of Royal Colleges of Physicians of the UK. It is the entry requirement for higher specialty training in internal medicine. The diploma has three parts: MRCP Part 1, MRCP Part 2 Written, and MRCP Part 2 Clinical (PACES).

Eligibility requires a primary medical qualification accepted by the GMC and a minimum of 12 months of postgraduate clinical experience before sitting Part 1. After passing Part 1, candidates can sit Part 2 Written or PACES in either order, or simultaneously.

MRCP Part 1 Details

FormatComputer-based (Surpass)
Structure2 papers in one day
Duration3 hours per paper
Questions100 best-of-five SBAs per paper (200 total)
MediaNo images
DeliveryTest centre (in-centre only from 2026 — remote online proctoring withdrawn in the UK)
Official source: mrcpuk.org ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • 12 months' postgraduate experience in medical employment.
  • No prior MRCP exams required to sit Part 1.

content:
MRCP Part 2 Overview

The MRCP(UK) Part 2 Written exam builds on the knowledge assessed in Part 1 and tests the acquisition of a representative sample of medical knowledge, skills and behaviour as specified in the UK Specialty Training Curriculum for Core Medical Training and the Curriculum for Internal Medicine.

Unlike Part 1, Part 2 Written includes clinical images, investigation findings and data interpretation. Candidates can sit Part 2 Written and PACES in either order, or simultaneously in the same assessment period.

MRCP Part 2 Details

FormatComputer-based (Surpass)
Structure2 papers in one day
Duration3 hours per paper
Questions100 best-of-five SBAs per paper (200 total)
MediaIncludes clinical images
DeliveryTest centre (in-centre only from 2026 — remote online proctoring withdrawn in the UK)
Official source: mrcpuk.org ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Must have passed MRCP(UK) Part 1.
  • Open to physicians in training as specified in the UK Specialty Training Curriculum.

content:
MRCS Part A Overview

Membership of the Royal College of Surgeons (MRCS) is an intercollegiate exam for surgical trainees who wish to become a member of one of the four surgical royal colleges in the UK and Ireland - the Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh, England, the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Glasgow, and the Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland.

The examination syllabus and the format are common to all four colleges. Candidates can enter through any college but only one college at each sitting. MRCS has two parts: Part A (MCQ) and Part B (OSCE). Candidates must pass Part A before applying for Part B.

MRCS Part A Details

FormatSingle best answer MCQ
Structure2 papers in one day
Paper 1Applied Basic Sciences - 180 questions, 3 hours
Paper 2Principles of Surgery in General - 120 questions, 2 hours
AttemptsUp to 6 attempts allowed
Official source: rcseng.ac.uk ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • A primary medical qualification acceptable to the UK GMC or the Medical Council in Ireland.
  • Check qualification acceptability via the World Directory of Medical Schools.

content:
MRCGP AKT Overview

The MRCGP examination is the postgraduate medical qualification required to attain a Certificate of Completion of Training (CCT) in General Practice. The MRCGP has three components: Workplace Based Assessments (WPBAs), the Applied Knowledge Test (AKT), and the Clinical Skills Assessment (CSA).

The AKT specifically tests the knowledge base behind independent general practice in the UK within the context of the NHS.

MRCGP AKT Details

FormatComputer-based assessment
Duration2 hours 40 minutes (160 minutes)
Questions160 questions
AttemptsMaximum 4 attempts (in GP training by 1 August 2023); 6 attempts if entering GP training on or after 2 August 2023
Official source: rcgp.org.uk ↗

Content breakdown

Content AreaWeighting
Clinical knowledge80%
Evidence-based practice10%
Primary care organisation & management10%

Eligibility & Requirements

  • You can take the AKT during or after the ST2 stage of GP training.
  • Review the GP curriculum on the RCGP website before sitting.

MRCEM Primary Overview

The MRCEM comprises three components: MRCEM Primary, MRCEM Intermediate SBA, and MRCEM OSCE. All MRCEM components are blueprinted to the RCEM 2021 Emergency Medicine Curriculum.

The MRCEM Primary is machine-marked with no negative marking. The pass mark is determined using the Angoff method.

MRCEM Primary Details

FormatComputer-based test (CBT)
Duration3 hours (180 minutes)
Questions180 single best answer questions
Marking1 mark per correct answer, no negative marking
AttemptsMaximum 6 attempts

Official source: rcem.ac.uk ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • No previous experience in Emergency Medicine is required.
  • Hold a medical qualification approved by the GMC for the purposes of registration.

content:
FRCA Primary Overview

The FRCA (Fellowship of the Royal College of Anaesthetists) examinations test the skills, knowledge and behaviour of doctors in training. The FRCA consists of two parts: Primary examinations (aligned to the core level training curriculum) and Final examinations (aligned to the intermediate level training curriculum).

The Primary FRCA has three components: an MCQ examination (covered here), an OSCE (16–19 stations), and a Structured Oral Examination (SOE).

FRCA Primary Details

FormatComputer-based test (CBT)
Duration3 hours (180 minutes)
Questions90 single best answer (SBA) questions
MarkingNo negative marking; Angoff pass mark
AttemptsMaximum 6 attempts
Official source: rcoa.ac.uk ↗

Content breakdown

SubjectNumber of questions
Pharmacology30
Physiology & biochemistry30
Physics, clinical measurement & statistics30

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Registered with the GMC or other National Medical Council.
  • Currently registered with the RCoA as a UK trainee in Anaesthesia, ACCS, Foundation, ICM, or as an Anaesthetist with the College of Anaesthetists of Ireland.
  • OR registered with the College in a recognised membership category (not affiliated).
  • OR has previously been granted Temporary Examination Eligibility (TEE).
  • Has not exceeded the maximum of six attempts.

content:
FRCA Final Overview

The Final FRCA is the second of the two Fellowship examinations of the Royal College of Anaesthetists and is aligned to the intermediate level training curriculum. Passing the Primary FRCA is a prerequisite for entry.

The Final FRCA has two components: a Written examination (a Multiple Choice Question paper and a Constructed Response Question / Short Answer Question paper) and a Structured Oral Examination (SOE). This question bank covers the single best answer (SBA) and multiple choice component of the Written exam.

FRCA Final Details

FormatWritten (MCQ paper + CRQ paper, on different days) and SOE
DurationCRQ paper: 3 hours (12 constructed response questions); MCQ paper: 3 hours (180 minutes) — sat on different days
QuestionsSingle best answer (SBA) only — multiple true/false (MTF) items were removed in September 2023
MarkingNo negative marking; Angoff pass mark
AttemptsMaximum 6 attempts
Official source: rcoa.ac.uk ↗

Content breakdown

DomainFocus
Clinical anaesthesiaPeri-operative, regional & subspecialty practice
Intensive care medicineCritical care management
Pain medicineAcute & chronic pain
Applied basic sciencesPharmacology, physiology, physics & clinical measurement

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Passed the Primary FRCA examination.
  • Registered with the RCoA in an appropriate training or membership category.
  • At the intermediate level training stage (or equivalent) in Anaesthesia.
  • Has not exceeded the maximum of six attempts.

content:
MSRA Overview

The Multi-Specialty Recruitment Assessment (MSRA) is a single computer-based exam comprising a Professional Dilemmas (PD) paper and a Clinical Problem Solving (CPS) paper. It is intended to assess candidates with a foundation level of competence.

The MSRA is used in selection for community sexual and reproductive health, general practice, neurosurgery, obstetrics and gynaecology, ophthalmology, psychiatry, and radiology training.

All MSRA assessments are held in Pearson VUE assessment centres.

MSRA Details

FormatComputer-based (Pearson VUE)
Structure2 papers
Paper 1 (PD)50 questions in 95 minutes
Paper 2 (CPS)86 questions in 75 minutes
PD contentProfessional integrity, coping with pressure, empathy & sensitivity
CPS contentSBA and EMQ across 12 clinical topic areas in general medicine
Official source: specialtytraining.hee.nhs.uk ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Eligibility is assessed during specialty training application.
  • Eligible applicants are invited to sit the MSRA.
  • You must book an appointment in time, or your application will not progress.

content:
MRCPsych Paper A Overview

MRCPsych Paper A is a written paper on the scientific and theoretical basis of psychiatry, covering Behavioural Science and Sociocultural Psychiatry, Human Development, Basic Neurosciences, Clinical Psychopharmacology, and Classification and Assessment in Psychiatry.

Once the first written component is passed, candidates have a time limit of 6 years (2,191 days) from the date that result was published to complete all remaining MRCPsych components, including the CASC. Failure to complete in this period means re-sitting both Paper A and Paper B before the CASC.

MRCPsych Paper A Details

FormatPearson VUE, computer-based (test centre or OnVUE remote invigilation)
Duration3 hours (180 minutes)
Questions150 questions
Composition~⅔ MCQ, ~⅓ extended matching items (EMI)
Time limit6 years (2,191 days) to complete all MRCPsych after first written pass
Maximum attempts6 attempts at any one MRCPsych component
Official source: rcpsych.ac.uk ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • You are eligible if you are a fully registered medical practitioner.
  • Review the full eligibility instructions on the RCPsych website.

MRCOG Part 1 Overview

There is no minimum score required for each paper - outcome is determined only by a candidate's overall combined mark.

Structure2 papers in one day

Questions100 SBAs per paper (200 total)
AttemptsMaximum 6 attempts (for UK Specialist Register candidates)
Official source: rcog.org.uk ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Two-stage application: eligibility application must be approved before booking.
  • Booking is made online after eligibility approval.

content:
MRCOG Part 2 Overview

The MRCOG Part 2 Examination assesses a candidate's ability to apply knowledge in clinical scenarios pertinent to obstetrics and gynaecology. Successful completion is required before progressing to the MRCOG Part 3 Examination.

The exam consists of two papers, each contributing 50% to the final score. Within each paper, SBAs account for 40% of marks and EMQs for 60%. A combined pass mark is determined through standard-setting for each exam - there is no separate pass mark for SBAs and EMQs.

MRCOG Part 2 Details

FormatComputer-based test (CBT)
Structure2 papers, each 50% of final score
Duration3 hours (180 minutes) per paper
Composition40% SBA + 60% EMQ in each paper
Suggested timing70 min SBAs / 110 min EMQs per paper
Official source: rcog.org.uk ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Must have passed the MRCOG Part 1 Examination.
  • Enrolled in an O&G training programme or have equivalent training and experience.
  • Training must align with the Capabilities in Practice (CiPs) and Knowledge Requirements in the MRCOG Syllabus Curriculum 2019.

content:
MRCPCH FOP & TAS Overview

The MRCPCH theory comprises three exams - Foundation of Practice (FOP), Theory and Science (TAS), and Applied Knowledge in Practice (AKP) - followed by a Clinical OSCE.

Theory exams can be taken in any order and are non-sequential, with three sittings per year. Candidates must pass all three theory examinations before attempting the MRCPCH Clinical examination.

This question bank covers both FOP and TAS in a single integrated resource.

MRCPCH FOP/TAS Details

FormatComputer-based test (CBT)
FOP duration2 hours (120 minutes)
FOP questions100 SBA questions
TAS duration2 hours (120 minutes)
TAS questions100 SBA questions
AttemptsUp to 6 attempts per theory exam
Official source: rcpch.ac.uk ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Hold a Primary Medical Qualification (PMQ) from a registered institution.
  • Hold a qualification recognised by the GMC UK.
  • After 6 failed attempts, additional educational evidence required by RCPCH.

content:
FRCOphth Part 1 Overview

The FRCOphth Part 1 Examination assesses a candidate's understanding of patient investigations and knowledge of basic and clinical sciences relevant to ophthalmology. It is a prerequisite for progression in ophthalmic specialist training.

Based on the learning outcomes from the first two years of the Ophthalmic Specialist Training (OST) curriculum, the exam covers basic sciences, theoretical optics, and some pathology.

FRCOphth Part 1 Details

ModeOnline Proctored Examination (home or workplace)
Structure2 MCQ papers on the same day
Duration2 hours per paper
Questions90 MCQs per paper
Break1-hour lunch break between papers
AttemptsMaximum 6 attempts
Official source: rcophth.ac.uk ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Hold a medical qualification approved by the GMC (UK) or the IMC (Ireland).
  • No previous experience in ophthalmology required to sit Part 1.
  • Must pass Part 1 before entering the third year of ophthalmic specialist training.

content:
Dentistry Exams: MFDS, ORE & LDS

This question bank covers preparation for three key dental examinations: Membership of the Faculty of Dental Surgery (MFDS), the Overseas Registration Examination (ORE), and the Licence in Dental Surgery (LDS).

The MFDS is an internationally recognised postgraduate qualification that demonstrates completion of foundation or basic postgraduate dental training. The ORE is administered by the General Dental Council for overseas-qualified dentists seeking UK registration. The LDS is the oldest continuously existing dental qualification in the UK. Note: RCSEd has announced that MFDS itself is changing across 2026–27 to a new tri-collegiate format — check the current specification before you book.

Dentistry (MFDS) Details

MFDS Part 1180 SBAs over 3 hours (written)
MFDS Part 2OSCE - 10 examined stations
ORE Part 1CBT covering dental sciences, law & ethics
ORE Part 2Practical clinical skills exam
LDS Part 1Written - dental sciences and ethics
LDS Part 2Practical clinical skills exam — changes to a 12-station OSCE plus six 20-minute Structured Clinical Reasoning cases over two days from Summer 2026
LDS Part 3180-minute operative assessment on a dental manikin
Official source: rcseng.ac.uk ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • MFDS: Hold a primary dental qualification and typically be registered to practise in your country of residence.
  • ORE/LDS: Demonstrate at least 1,600 hours of dental clinical experience.

content:
Medical Finals & UKMLA AKT Overview

Our question repository comprises more than 6,000 Single Best Answer Questions catering to students preparing for finals and the MLA exam.

All medical students graduating from UK universities from the 2024–25 academic year onwards must pass the MLA as part of their degree before joining the medical register. International doctors seeking UK practice (previously taking PLAB) now take the MLA from 2024 onwards.

The UKMLA has two components: the AKT (Applied Knowledge Test) - an on-screen multiple-choice exam with 150–200 SBAs set by the GMC - and the CPSA (Clinical and Professional Skills Assessment), an OSCE with real-life scenarios including mock consultations and acute ward settings.

Medical Student Finals Details

FormatOn-screen multiple-choice (AKT)
Questions150–200 single best answers
Test setterSet by the GMC
CPSA componentOSCE with real-life clinical scenarios
IMG CPSA venueGMC clinical assessment centre, Manchester
First sitting2024–25 academic year onwards (UK graduates)
Official source: gmc-uk.org ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Required for all UK medical school graduates from 2024–25 onwards.
  • Required for international medical graduates wishing to practise in the UK (replaces PLAB from 2024).

content:
PLAB 1 Overview

The Professional and Linguistic Assessments Board (PLAB) test is the main route by which international medical graduates demonstrate they have the knowledge and skills to practise medicine in the UK. It is run by the General Medical Council (GMC).

PLAB 1 is a written examination of single best answer questions covering the application of clinical knowledge to the care of patients. It is mapped to the same content areas as the UK Medical Licensing Assessment (UKMLA). Passing PLAB 1 is required before sitting the PLAB 2 practical assessment.

PLAB 1 Details

FormatWritten, single best answer (SBA)
Duration3 hours (180 minutes)
Questions180 single best answer (SBA) questions
MarkingNo negative marking; pass mark set by the GMC
DeliveryTest centres worldwide and in the UK
Official source: gmc-uk.org ↗

What it tests

AreaFocus
Clinical managementDiagnosis, investigation & treatment across specialties
Acute & emergency careRecognising and managing the unwell patient
Prescribing & safetySafe, effective prescribing and patient safety
Professional practiceEthics, law and communication in UK practice

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Hold a primary medical qualification the GMC accepts.
  • Meet the GMC’s English language requirement (IELTS or OET).
  • Intending to apply for GMC registration with a licence to practise via the PLAB route.
